summary: Iteration 17 (laddered moonbag exit) tested end-to-end. Created /app/backend/tests/test_exit_ladder_it17.py with 51 tests: 20 pure state-machine tests (parse_ladder, evaluate_ladder, record_milestone_hit, ratchet, arming, rug_stop, time_limit, one-step-per-eval), 16 integration tests across graduation_executor (mocked jupiter.get_quote + execute_swap) and pumpfun_autobuy (mocked _pumpportal_build_tx/_sign_and_send/_current_curve_price), plus API shape + 15-endpoint regression sweep. Full suite run: 158/158 passed (test_pumpfun_antirug 79 + it14 + it15 + it16 28 + it17 51). Frontend verified on the public URL: both panels render the ladder string and rug stop, TP/SL advisory lines removed, partial_sell events render with purple badge and ratio/peak/floor/sold%/remaining%. No live trading flags were enabled; no real PumpPortal/Jupiter/RPC calls made.

minor.issue: Makes TWO RPC round-trips per call: _check_curve_state() for virtual_sol_reserves then _check_curve_state_full() for virtual_token_reserves. Doubles RPC cost per position per monitor tick and mixes reserves read at two different slots (slightly inconsistent price). _check_curve_state_full already returns virtual_sol_reserves — use it alone.

If the bonding-curve read fails at buy time entry_price stays 0.0, so _evaluate_position can never compute a ratio and the position gets NO ladder/rug-stop protection — only the time_limit_no_quote exit at hold_max_seconds. Consider a lazy re-derivation of entry_price or aborting/flagging the buy when entry price is unknown.

record_milestone_hit resets floor_armed=False on every ratchet, and re-arming requires peak_ratio >= new_milestone.mult * 1.05 (e.g. >= 21x for the 20x milestone). If price touches exactly 20.0x and immediately dumps, the old (already armed) 5x floor is discarded, the new 10x floor never arms, and rug_stop is disabled after the first milestone -> position has no downside exit until hold_max_seconds. Suggest arming against the floor itself (floor * 1.05) or carrying over the armed flag when peak already clears the new floor.

The arming loop matches the milestone by `abs(m.floor_after - state.current_floor) < 1e-9`. If two milestones are configured with the same floor_after the wrong (lower-mult) milestone is matched and the floor arms too early. Prefer keying the arm threshold off the highest hit milestone index.

ratio is derived from a Jupiter quote sized at the FULL remaining token balance, so price impact is baked into the ratio; large positions will read a systematically lower multiple than the true mark price (milestones fire late). Acceptable as conservative, but worth documenting.

PumpPortal 'XX%' is a percentage of the CURRENT wallet balance for that mint, while remaining_pct_of_original is tracked multiplicatively in memory. Any external balance change or partial fill silently desyncs the two, and the <0.5% dust rule then decides closure from a stale number.

ui_bugs.issue: partial_sell reason is rendered TWICE — once as purple text (`p.reason && p.event === 'partial_sell'`) and again unconditionally further down (`p.reason` in amber). Verified live: 'milestone_5x_sell_80pct' and 'milestone_20x_sell_50pct' each appear 2x in the event row.

Stale text still advertises the removed TP/SL policy: line ~110 'then Jupiter-route buy with real TP/SL.' and footer line ~334 'Real TP/SL via Jupiter reverse quotes.' Should reference the laddered exit + trailing floor.
Graduation partial_sell docs carry `tokens_remaining` but the UI never renders it, while PumpfunPanel shows `remaining: X%`. Inconsistent — grad users can't see how much moonbag is left.

issues: The ladder string wraps to 3 lines inside a single 5-column grid cell, making that config row ~3x taller than its neighbours and leaving a ragged block. Consider giving the Ladder cell col-span-2/3 or rendering the milestones as chips.

action_items: De-duplicate the partial_sell `reason` rendering in PumpfunPanel.jsx (~line 280 vs 325) and GraduationPanel.jsx (~line 298 vs 315).
Collapse _current_curve_price to a single _check_curve_state_full RPC call.

Close the trailing-floor arming gap after a ratchet (arm off floor*1.05, or preserve armed state when peak already clears the new floor) — currently a position can be fully unprotected between milestone N and peak >= milestone(N).mult*1.05.
Handle entry_price == 0.0 (curve read failed at buy) so the ladder is not silently disabled for that position.
Update GraduationPanel copy that still says 'real TP/SL' and optionally render tokens_remaining/remaining% for graduation partial sells.
critical_code_review_comments: record_milestone_hit correctly ratchets floor UP only and is only invoked after a confirmed sell in BOTH bots — verified by test that a failed execute_swap/_sign_and_send leaves milestones_hit and token/remaining accounting untouched (sell_failed event only). Good fail-safe design.

evaluate_ladder does not mutate milestones_hit, so a caller that forgets record_milestone_hit would loop-sell the same milestone forever. Both current call sites are correct, but a defensive guard/log would be cheap insurance.

graduation ratio normalization by frac_remaining = tokens_out/tokens_original is correct: after an 80% sell at a flat price the ratio still reads 5.0x (verified in test_ratio_normalized_after_partial).
pumpfun_autobuy.py is 938 lines and graduation_executor.py 520 — pumpfun_autobuy should be split (curve-reads / safety filters / execution) per the >700-line guideline.

Milestone boundaries are strict `ratio >= mult`; float noise in the quote path (observed 99.99999999999999 for a nominal 100x) can defer the final milestone by one tick. Harmless in production but worth a tiny epsilon if exactness matters.

rca_of_the_issue: Duplicate reason text: both panels added a partial_sell-specific purple `{p.reason}` span without removing the pre-existing unconditional amber `{p.reason}` span, so every partial_sell row prints the milestone reason twice. Trailing-floor gap: record_milestone_hit unconditionally sets floor_armed=False on ratchet while evaluate_ladder's arm condition is peak >= milestone.mult*1.05, so a ratio that touches a milestone exactly and reverses can never re-arm the newly ratcheted floor, and rug_stop is already disabled once any milestone is hit.
